what_this_is: the set of mechanical or sweep edits this repository has made, each with the changed-line count that was expected BEFORE it ran and the count it actually produced. Enforced by tests/test_diff01_blast_radius_g14.py.
why_a_register_and_not_a_diff_review: the EOL-02 first pass changed 9,832 lines to fix 68 -- 145 times its intent -- and the suite was green before and after, because every file was individually correct. Correct-per-file and catastrophic-in-aggregate are the same operation for a codemod, and no guard in this repository measured aggregate. A reviewer reading the diffstat caught it, which is not a mechanism.

thresholds.halt_ratio_meaning: actual / expected. Above this the edit halts and is reported, whatever the suite says.
thresholds.sweep_shaped_meaning: a commit touching at least this many files is sweep-shaped and must appear here, by commit_subject, if it lands at or after the enactment commit. The count is the signature of a mechanical edit: hand edits are deep and narrow, codemods are shallow and wide.

enacted_at_subject: g14: DIFF-01 -- a sweep edit states its blast radius before it runs
scope_note: commits BEFORE the enactment commit are out of scope, following DOC-07's own design: R-4 makes history uncorrectable and a guard that fails on history nobody can fix is a guard people switch off. The generation-13 EOL-02 sweep is registered below as the founding entry and is used by the guard as its positive control from history.

entries.description: add an explicit newline= to every text-mode write in src/, scripts/ and tests/. The keyword was added correctly at every site; the files were then written back through Python's own text mode, which normalised 25 CRLF files to LF.
entries.expected_basis: the AST scan found 68 violating call sites; one line changes at each.

entries.description: the same edit redone over bytes, asserting per file that its CRLF and LF counts are unchanged.
entries.expected_basis: unchanged from the first pass: 68 call sites, one line each.
entries.commit_subject: g13: EOL-02 -- every text-mode write states its line ending
entries.commit_changed_lines_note: the commit is larger than the sweep because it also carries the new rule text in docs/RULES_ENACTED.md and the new guard module. The sweep itself is the 68 above; DIFF-01 governs the sweep, not the commit it travels in.

entries.description: MECH-01 pass 4 landing: the runner, the mechanism description, its guard, one interpolation-allowlist entry, and the six pre-registered artefacts.
entries.commit_subject: g14: MECH-01 pass 4 -- a null matched on row count, and what it returned
entries.why_not_mechanical: no file was edited by a script. It is wide because new modules and their artefacts land together, which is depth-1 breadth rather than a sweep.

entries.description: the close ruling of 2026-08-29 enacted: the PRE-01 register, checker, guard and rule text; the terminal loop state and its writer; the README badge; a superseding note in the audit master; and the changelog entry.
entries.commit_subject: close: the ruling enacted -- PRE-01, the accession record, and EXT-04's remote
entries.why_not_mechanical: no file was edited by a script. Every change was made deliberately at its own site. It is wide because a rule enactment lands its register, its checker, its guard and its documentation together, which is depth-1 breadth rather than a sweep.
entries.registered_although_below_the_trigger: at nine files the commit sits exactly in the blind spot DIFF-01 states for itself -- 'a mechanical edit confined to nine files is invisible to it'. Adding this entry makes the commit ten files and therefore sweep-shaped, so the guard now sees what it is looking at. Declaring it is cheaper than a commit that is silent because it happened to be one file under the threshold.

kinds.mechanical: a codemod, normalisation or rule enactment applied across files by a script. DIFF-01 governs it and the full expected/actual accounting is required.
kinds.not-mechanical: a wide commit that is not a sweep -- typically new files landing together. It appears here because the file-count trigger cannot see intent, and it must say why it is not mechanical. This is the false-positive path the rule's stated limitation predicts, and declaring it is the intended response; splitting a commit to slip under the threshold would be gaming the guard.
